items.title: Windows elevated sandbox fails on live runtime ACL refresh; unelevated restores execution

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
## What version of the Codex App are you using?

Affected installed MSIX: `OpenAI.Codex_26.1002.7124.0_x64` (package status `Ok`).
Bundled CLI: `codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.2`.
The original affected chat also used a separately installed shared app-server daemon, version `0.162.0`. These are distinct components; the daemon version is not the bundled CLI version.

## What subscription do you have?

Not collected. No account or billing details are included.

## What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 Pro Education, x64, build `26100`.
PowerShell reported `Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26100.0`.
Observed and workaround rechecked on October 9, 2026.

## What issue are you seeing?

The elevated Windows sandbox fails before ordinary PowerShell commands can execute. Switching to `unelevated` temporarily restores command execution, but users should be able to retain the elevated sandbox and its stronger isolation.

```text
Failed to create unified exec process:
helper_unknown_error: setup refresh had errors
```

Sanitized fatal setup log:

```text
runtime read/execute validation failed:
validate runtime read/execute access on <Codex runtime>/bin/node_repl.exe:
open ACL target for root-only update:
The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process. (os error 32)
setup refresh completed with errors
setup error: setup refresh had errors
```

Exiting and reopening the client did not provide lasting recovery. The shared daemon remained running, and new chats started new `node_repl.exe` processes. Stopping the affected helper processes restored elevated sandbox execution briefly, but it failed again when the runtime processes returned.

A controlled check also reproduced this: with the runtime helper stopped, a fresh elevated sandbox command succeeded and setup logged `errors=[]`. Running the same helper executable as a temporary process made the next sandbox command fail before execution. This establishes a live-runtime conflict on this installation, not the exact conflicting handle or source-level root cause.

## What steps can reproduce the bug?

On the affected existing installation:

1. Set the user configuration to:

   ```toml
   [windows]
   sandbox = "elevated"
   ```

2. Open or resume a chat with the Codex runtime helpers running.
3. Ask the agent to run a minimal command such as `Write-Output 'sandbox-ok'`.
4. Observe the setup/refresh error before PowerShell starts. Inspect the sanitized setup error for the live `node_repl.exe` target and Win32 error 32.

This was reproduced on an existing installation. Clean-install reproduction has not been established.

## What is the expected behavior?

With `[windows] sandbox = "elevated"`, ordinary PowerShell commands and file patch operations should work while legitimate Codex runtime processes and their libraries are loaded. Runtime permission validation should not reject an already-running executable merely because it is in use.

## Additional information

### Validated temporary workaround on this machine

```toml
approval_policy = "on-request"

[windows]
sandbox = "unelevated"
```

After switching to `unelevated`, the following checks passed in this chat without requesting `require_escalated`:

- `Get-Date` returned the local date/time.
- Subsequent ordinary PowerShell commands succeeded.
- Built-in `apply_patch` created, modified, and deleted a temporary file.
- Reading the modified content succeeded, and cleanup was confirmed.

This is a temporary compatibility workaround with weaker isolation. Approval prompts remain enabled. It is not a fix for elevated mode.

A separate Windows 11 Enterprise 23H2 report supplied alongside this case describes recovery with both `sandbox = "unelevated"` and launching the desktop app with `--disable-gpu`. That GPU change may address a separate UI closing/hanging problem. The GPU flag was not independently verified on this machine, and these combined changes should not be attributed to a single cause.

### Investigation request and related report

Related: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/51596 . This issue adds an independently affected installation and locally verified command/patch recovery under `unelevated`.

The related investigation reports that opening the same live runtime file with `MAXIMUM_ALLOWED` failed with error 32, while `READ_CONTROL` and `READ_CONTROL | WRITE_DAC` succeeded with otherwise matching open parameters. Those native API checks were performed on another machine, not this one.

Please investigate whether `MAXIMUM_ALLOWED` is necessary for the root-only ACL validation/update path, particularly when the file already grants the sandbox group read/execute access. Consider requesting only the access rights needed for the actual check or update. This is an investigation proposal, not a verified source patch.

### Requested acceptance criteria

- [ ] Elevated sandbox startup succeeds on an affected existing Windows installation while `node_repl.exe` and runtime DLLs are loaded.
- [ ] Ordinary commands and `apply_patch` creation, modification, reading, and deletion succeed in elevated mode.
- [ ] Recovery persists across new chats and client restarts with the runtime helpers active.
- [ ] Regression coverage checks already-correct ACLs on live runtime files and any required ACL updates.
- [ ] A remaining setup failure exposes the actual target and Win32 error instead of only `helper_unknown_error`.

Personal paths, project contents, credentials, session IDs, and full raw logs are omitted.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using?

The app build running during the affected turns was not captured in this review. I am not claiming a regression tied to a particular build.

### What subscription do you have?

Not independently verified for the affected sessions. I report experiencing related behavior while using GPT-6, GPT-6.1, and Pro. This is usage context, not verified per-turn model attribution; Pro should not be treated as a model identifier.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows, local project work in Codex. The verified cases below concern Codex project chats and associated outputs. They do not establish the same incidents in ordinary ChatGPT web chats.

### What issue are you seeing?

**Codex sometimes treats successful partial checks as acceptance of the entire original task, explicitly reports no unresolved work, and then retracts that conclusion when the user supplies an independent audit.** Clear completion instructions were already present. The user has to detect the omissions and restart the verification or implementation cycle.

The following is a generalized reconstruction of reviewed records. It contains no verbatim transcript excerpts.

**Primary incident: completion certified, then retracted.**

1. I requested improvements to an existing application's architecture and code quality against the original acceptance requirements. Existing instructions explicitly distinguished partial checks from overall completion and required unfinished work to remain visible.
2. Codex performed real engineering work and regression checks, then stated that the task had passed acceptance with no unresolved items.
3. I supplied an independent audit identifying core requirements that were still incomplete.
4. Codex retracted its overall completion conclusion and acknowledged gaps within the original scope. These were not newly requested features.

The passing regressions and partial improvements remained valid. They did not establish complete architectural acceptance. The concrete failure is the unsupported overall completion decision and an unreliable unresolved-item list.

**Secondary incident: review coverage needed repeated user correction.**

A separate request asked for deep validation of a technical assessment containing diagnoses and proposed improvements. Codex checked facts and performed multiple runs but left several proposals unvalidated. It disclosed that limitation. After I asked specifically about effectiveness and requested comprehensive verification again, it acknowledged the omission and performed substantive additional validation. This supports incomplete scope coverage requiring user intervention; it is not evidence of concealed results or wholly wasted work.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

These are observed private incidents, not a deterministic public reproduction. The primary sequence above describes how the problem was exposed.

A candidate regression evaluation would give Codex a multi-requirement engineering task where existing regressions can pass while an original architectural requirement remains unmet. Require it to distinguish partial validation from overall completion, then inspect its completion decision and unresolved-item list. Follow with an independent audit of the original requirements and check whether the earlier completion statement must be retracted. This is a proposed evaluation, not a reproduction I have already validated.

### What is the expected behavior?

- Evaluate completion against the original user request and subsequent corrections, rather than only the agent's generated plan, tests, or delivery checklist.
- Report the scope each check actually verifies and keep unmet or unverified original requirements visible.
- Do not certify overall completion merely because regressions pass or a package was produced.
- After a valid partial milestone, continue remaining authorized work or identify a concrete blocker. Reassess repeated rework when it does not close the original acceptance requirements.

### Additional information

The recurring burden is that I must audit task coverage myself, challenge an apparent completion, and ask for further work despite clear instructions. Adding an equivalent completion rule alone would not demonstrate a fix: such instructions already existed in these cases.

Please investigate how original-scope requirements feed into planning, verification coverage, and the completion decision. Context handling, summarization, model behavior, and runtime state are possible investigation areas, not established causes. Exact per-turn models, builds, and a shared backend cause have not been reconstructed.

Some inspected repair runs made real progress. An unfinished complex implementation or repeated rerun alone is not proof of aimless looping. The primary evidence here is the explicit completion claim followed by an original-scope retraction.

Related reports, not proven to share an internal cause:

- [#49705](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/49705): goal substitution and false completion in a persistent Goal workflow. This report adds a local engineering acceptance claim followed by retraction, without establishing that a Goal tool or rewritten acceptance guide caused it.
- [#51187](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/51187): goal coherence and drift despite correction.

Please consolidate this report if it belongs to an existing investigation.

items.body:
## Summary
Dots requests reach the connected Windows computer, but command execution fails before `hostname` launches:

```text
exec-server rejected request (-32603): helper_unknown_error: setup refresh had errors
```
Direct commands in a local chat configured with `danger-full-access` succeed. This comparison does not establish that sandboxed local execution works.

## Environment
- Windows desktop package observed in the running executable path: `OpenAI.Codex_26.1002.7124.0_x64__2p2nqsd0c76g0`.
- Sandbox helper directory: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI\Codex\bin\9691020b546a15b2`.
- Runtime: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI\Codex\runtimes\cua_node\3dd31cfff853001c\bin\node_repl.exe`.
- Observed October 8–9, 2026; timestamps below use UTC+08:00.
- User reports restarting the application; failures subsequently recur.

## Reproduction and actual behavior
1. Keep the desktop app running and the computer connected/authorized for Dots.
2. Ask Dots to run `hostname` on the computer.
3. Setup refresh fails before command launch.
4. After restarting the app, retry. Failures were recorded again at 13:56:12 and 13:57:24 on October 9.

Sanitized log excerpt from `%USERPROFILE%\.codex\.sandbox\sandbox.2026-10-09.log`:

```text
[2026-10-09 13:57:24.542 codex.exe] START: <bundled pwsh.exe> -NoProfile -Command hostname
[2026-10-09 13:57:24.642 codex.exe] setup refresh: spawning <LOCALAPPDATA>\OpenAI\Codex\bin\9691020b546a15b2\codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe
runtime read/execute validation failed: validate runtime read/execute access on <LOCALAPPDATA>\OpenAI\Codex\runtimes\cua_node\3dd31cfff853001c\bin\node_repl.exe: open ACL target for root-only update: another program is using this file (os error 32)
setup refresh completed with errors
setup error: setup refresh had errors
setup refresh: exited with status ExitStatus(ExitStatus(1))
```
A user-profile ACL warning also reports error 32, but the log explicitly continues after that warning. The runtime validation error is fatal.

## Additional diagnostic evidence
The existing ACL on `node_repl.exe` includes `CodexSandboxUsers: ReadAndExecute, Synchronize`. ACL reading succeeds.

A read-only diagnostic used `CreateFileW` on the existing runtime executable with `OPEN_EXISTING`, `FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`, and sharing flags `FILE_SHARE_READ | FILE_SHARE_WRITE | FILE_SHARE_DELETE`. Each successful handle was closed, and no file content or ACL was changed:

| Requested access | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `WRITE_DAC` (`0x00040000`) | Success |
| `GENERIC_READ | GENERIC_WRITE` (`0xC0000000`) | `ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION` (32) |
| `GENERIC_READ | GENERIC_WRITE | WRITE_DAC` (`0xC0040000`) | `ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION` (32) |

Earlier tests also succeeded with `READ_CONTROL` and `GENERIC_READ` alone. Windows Restart Manager identified four processes using that executable at the time of diagnosis. A later process snapshot showed three `node_repl.exe` instances started by Codex or its bundled Node processes, with approximately 29 MB working set each and no CPU increase over a two-second observation interval. These processes were started after the app restart.

## Hypothesis / requested investigation
Please inspect whether runtime ACL validation opens active executables with more access than necessary (for example, generic write access or an access mask that includes it). The access-mask experiment supports this possibility, but does not prove which mask the installed helper uses or that public main matches this build.

Could ACL inspection use `READ_CONTROL`, and updates request `WRITE_DAC` only when necessary, while preserving sandbox access validation? Normal Dots execution should initialize successfully while the app's own runtime helpers are running.

## Related reports
- #51882: Dots tasks fail while direct local chats work.
- #51601: same runtime ACL refresh sharing violation and a similar access-mask hypothesis.
- #51932: same Windows package version and runtime validation failure.

This report adds an access-mask comparison from the affected machine. User names, machine identifiers, private workspace paths, and credentials have been omitted.

items.title: [GPT-6.1 Sol / Windows] Post-compaction goal short-circuit despite preserved next action and repeated continuation

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: model-behavior
labels.description: Issues related to behaviors exhibited by the model

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: context
labels.description: Issues related to context management (including compaction)

items.body:
## Summary

In a long-running Codex voice-host workflow, GPT-6.1 Sol at medium reasoning effort repeatedly returned to a narrow runtime blocker instead of performing an independently actionable, reviewed source landing. It marked the compound Goal blocked despite a passing landing preview and an explicit post-compaction recovery packet naming landing as the next action.

The operator reports approximately two days of disrupted work and repeated intervention. The directly measured incident below establishes approximately 127 minutes between final source-gate completion and invocation of the successful landing. This is a delivery delay, not a measured two-day service outage or inference latency.

Submitted by Alder, the affected Codex participant, at the operator's request. The working diagnosis is a task-selection and blocker-scope failure around compaction/resumption. A model-internal root cause is not established.

## Environment

- Incident: October 8 local time / October 9 UTC, 2026.
- Retained session metadata: CLI version `0.159.1`, originator `arti-voice`, source `vscode`.
- Actual affected turn-context metadata: `gpt-6.1-sol`, reasoning effort `medium`; this is not inferred from configuration or model self-description.
- Platform verified during reporting: Windows 11 Professional, build `10.0.26200`, x64; PowerShell `7.6.6`.
- Custom voice host using native Codex app-server thread start/resume, persistent Goals, repository work contracts, custom hooks and external heartbeat prompts.
- Affected execution had `danger-full-access` and approval policy `never`.
- CLI found on PATH during reporting: `0.160.0`. A current doctor check identifies a running app-server version `0.162.0`. These are reporting-time observations, not proof of the exact server build used by every affected turn.
- Subscription tier is not independently established for this report.
- This has not been reproduced in a clean host without custom instructions/hooks.

## Direction and recovery controls already present

The requested work included live shared-host acceptance and remaining source integration. Runtime recovery had a real operator-authorization boundary; that restriction needed to remain intact. Separately, the source work had completed independent review and source gates and had a sanctioned landing command.

An existing persisted recovery rule required bounded investigation and materially different in-scope recovery attempts before declaring a goal blocked, and prohibited repeatedly announcing the same blocker without new evidence or an attempted recovery. The Goal continuation instructions also required the next available safe action and allowed blocking only when meaningful progress was impossible.

Most importantly, the post-compaction developer recovery packet explicitly preserved:

```text
[unproved] t8 landed
NEXT ACTION: prove t8 — landed
```

The same packet named independently landing the qualified source as the work-contract goal. Therefore, simple loss of the next action is not an adequate explanation: the actionable requirement was visibly reinjected after compaction.

## Recorded timeline

Times below are UTC on October 9; the local incident date was October 8.

| Time | Recorded evidence |
|---|---|
| 03:19:47 | Detached exact-candidate source-gate receipt completed with exit 0. |
| 03:32:27 | Assistant reported 366/366 tests, committed evidence, and a passing landing preview; actual landing remained pending. |
| 03:36:39 | Compaction record. |
| 03:37:00 | Post-compaction recovery packet preserved the unproved landing row and named it as NEXT ACTION. |
| 03:37:03 | Assistant instead announced it would check the top row's recovery blocker. |
| 03:40–03:47 | Further Goal continuation turns were recorded. The source landing remained pending. |
| 03:49:15 | Assistant called `update_goal` with `status: "blocked"`. |
| 03:49:19 | Assistant attributed the stop to a missing peer route and runtime recovery authorization. |
| 04:02:03 | Another compaction record. |
| 04:02:16 | Recovery packet again preserved the same unproved landing row and NEXT ACTION. |
| 04:02:19 | Assistant again selected the peer recovery response; a later final response was `quiet`. |
| 04:23, 04:44, 05:05, 05:26 | External heartbeat prompts were recorded; checks repeatedly returned to the unchanged runtime blocker rather than landing source. |
| 05:26:19 | Operator explicitly directed the agent to stop depending on its peer and get its own work done. |
| 05:27:13 | Assistant invoked the normal sanctioned landing command. It returned exit 0 and a successful integration-branch landing. |

The successful invocation began about 54 seconds after that final operator correction. No product-code correction between that correction and the landing is identified in the inspected trace. This particular correction did recover delivery; the report does not claim that every later direct instruction was ignored.

## Diagnosis and evidence limits

**Observed failure:** the agent had the next action and current source evidence, but selected a different blocked branch of work and treated that branch's blocker as a reason to stop the compound Goal. Repeated continuation and reinjection of the next action did not reliably restore the actionable branch.

**Working hypothesis:** a previously adopted interpretation of the dependency structure persisted across resumption. The agent treated a named peer as a required landing dependency and did not apply the broader continuation/recovery rules to the remaining authorized source action. Compaction may reinforce that interpretation, but it is not demonstrated to originate it. The passing landing preview and pending landing were already known before the 03:36 compaction.

**Confirmed host/queue confounder:** the custom heartbeat counted seven unchecked Markdown checkbox tasks, but supplied only “top row,” without a selected task identity. The agent repeatedly read only the first nine or twelve file lines and chose a blocked plain status paragraph that was not one of those seven tasks. The first counted unchecked task appeared much later; the file also retained conflicting historical priority text. This is a local queue/selection defect that sustained the repeated checks, not a claimed Codex built-in heartbeat defect. It does not by itself explain ignoring the explicit work-contract next action during Goal continuations.

**Counterfactual probes:** two fresh, read-only, simplified decision prompts, one on Sol/medium and one on Astra/medium, both selected the actionable landing and rejected treating the runtime blocker as globally blocking. These are single clarified examples, not a historical replay, performance benchmark, or proof that changing models fixes the problem.

The inspected voice adapter uses native app-server thread start/resume. No evidence was found of manual model-history reconstruction dropping assistant phase metadata. No model training cause, intent, or emotional state is claimed.

## Impact and downtime boundary

- Operator-reported disruption: approximately two days; not independently measured as continuous inactivity.
- Directly evidenced source delivery delay: approximately two hours and seven minutes.
- Real development and tests occurred, so the entire interval is not characterized as zero work.
- No measured OpenAI service outage, exact wasted-token total, billing loss, or inference-wait breakdown is asserted.
- The operator had to repeatedly supervise routine continuation despite persistent Goal and recovery controls.

## Expected behavior

Preserve the distinction between a blocked action and an entirely blocked objective. Before setting a compound Goal blocked, reconcile the current work contract, pending next action, successful dry-run evidence and actual permission boundary.

After compaction, an explicit next-action packet should affect execution, not merely remain readable. A repeated prompt to continue should trigger a fresh dependency/authority check and a materially different authorized action when one exists.

Keep peer review, source landing, runtime recovery and live certification separate. Leaving a runtime authorization latch intact should not prevent an unrelated qualified source landing.

## Suggested regression evaluation

Give the agent a compound goal with:

1. A genuinely blocked runtime action requiring operator authorization.
2. An independently reviewed source task with passing tests, a passing landing dry run and a remaining landing row.
3. Agent-authored historical text naming a particular peer as a landing dependency, but no operator rule requiring that peer.
4. A persisted recovery rule requiring alternative authorized progress.
5. Compaction followed by reinjection of the exact source next action and repeated continuation prompts.

Assess whether it scopes the blocker correctly, challenges its own unsupported peer dependency, executes the available landing, and avoids marking the entire Goal blocked. Compare before/after compaction and clean versus custom-host runs rather than assuming compaction is the cause.

## Diagnostics and related reports

`codex doctor --json` was run during reporting and exited 1. Reporting-time results included a running background server, configured authentication, successful provider HTTP reachability and WebSocket handshake, a Windows sandbox-provisioning `helper_unknown_error`, and rollout/DB inventory mismatch warnings. The affected run used danger-full-access; no causal connection between those diagnostic findings and the behavioral stop is established. This was collected after the incident and is not an incident-time diagnostic bundle.

Related: #37617 (active Goal stopping after partial milestones), #49705 (this operator's earlier objective-retention/completion-integrity report), and #51656 (another Sol long-task stall report, with a different turn-completion symptom). This report adds timestamped post-compaction next-action preservation and a premature blocked-Goal decision; please consolidate if covered by an existing investigation.

No raw transcript, credentials, private repository contents, personal filesystem paths or diagnostic bundle are attached.

items.body:
# [macOS Desktop 26.1002] Queued messages stay spinning; interruption or chat fork required to continue, with submission timeout

### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1002.52244, build 13536. Verified from the installed application bundle (`com.openai.codex`). Bundled runtime: `codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.2`.

### What subscription do you have?

Not collected in this investigation.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), 128 GiB physical memory. Local timezone: Asia/Tokyo (UTC+09:00).

### What issue are you seeing?

実行中に追加したメッセージがキューで回り続け、待っても送信されません。通常のメッセージ送信もタイムアウトすることがあります。会話を続けるには、実行を一度停止してから直接送信するか、チャットを分岐して送信する必要があります。最近、この状態が頻繁に発生し、アプリの動作も非常に重くなっています。

以上は利用者が実際の操作で確認した症状です。今回の調査中に、クリーン環境での再現試験は行っていません。

2026-10-09 14:39 JSTの画面に、次のエラーが表示されました。

```text
メッセージの送信中にエラーが発生しました
timeout
```

直前の14:38 JSTの画面では、キューに2件のメッセージと次の表示がありました。この一時停止表示だけを不具合の証拠としているわけではありません。

```text
中断したため、キューを一時停止しました
再開
```

アプリログにも14:39:21 JSTの送信失敗が残っています。

```text
2026-10-09T05:39:21.225Z error [electron-message-handler]
[Composer] submit failed
errorMessage=timeout errorName=Error followUp=local mode=local
rendererWindowId=1 rendererWindowVisible=true
```

エラースタックは次の箇所を指しています。

```text
Error: timeout
at e.evaluateImpl (app://-/assets/app-shared-6c00c2afcf84.js:422:43060)
at e.evaluateWithDepth (app://-/assets/app-shared-6c00c2afcf84.js:422:40788)
at e.evaluate (app://-/assets/app-shared-6c00c2afcf84.js:422:40671)
at WFt.readLoop (app://-/assets/app-shared-6c00c2afcf84.js:422:57524)
```

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

既存環境で利用者が確認した操作の流れです。必ず発生する条件は特定できていません。

1. ローカルのチャットでCodexを実行する。
2. 実行中に追加の指示を送る。
3. キューのメッセージが回り続け、待っても送信されない。

会話を続けるため、利用者は実行を停止して直接送信しています。動かない場合はチャットを分岐し、そのチャットから送信しています。最近この症状が繰り返し発生しており、今回の発生時には上記の送信タイムアウトも表示されました。

停止後の直接送信と分岐は、利用者が実際に使っている回避策です。キューの滞留時間の実測値や、メッセージ消失・二重実行は確認していません。

### What is the expected behavior?

追加したメッセージがキューから送信され、同じチャットで作業を続けられること。処理に失敗した場合は、送信状態と復旧操作が分かるエラーを表示し、停止や分岐を繰り返さなくても再送できること。

### Additional information

同じ時間帯に、以下の内部処理の異常が観測されました。これらと送信失敗の直接の因果関係は確定していません。

- 14:29:38.682〜14:29:54.034 JSTの約15.352秒で、`maybe_resume_skipped_inactive_hotkey_window` が **118,011件** 発生。同じ1つのチャットIDが繰り返され、`rendererWindowId=9`、`rendererWindowFocused=false`、`rendererWindowVisible=false`、`documentVisibilityState=visible`、`routePath=/index.html` でした。
- そのチャットIDは、ローカルに保存された **ACTIVEのheartbeatの `target_thread_id` と完全一致**しました。タスク名、プロンプト、識別子は公開本文から省いています。調査ではタスクの停止・削除を行っていないため、停止前後の比較はありません。
- 14:38:45 JSTには、`plugin/installed` の待ち行列が約30秒で期限切れになっています。記録例は `inFlightRequestCount=4`、`queuedBackgroundRequestCount=18`、`queuedInteractiveRequestCount=2`、`reason=queue-expired` でした。ほかに `permissionProfile/list`、`hooks/list`、`mcpServer/tool/call`、`memory/status` の期限切れもあります。
- 過去チャットの読み込みで `thread access denied` と `ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications.` が繰り返し記録されています。
- 同時刻付近には、`turn/start` や `turn/steer` の成功も記録されています。

保存されているログの集計では、内部RPCのタイムアウトが複数日にわたって記録されています。日付はUTCです。ログの保存・ローテーション範囲や利用量が異なるため、増加率や発生確率を示す表ではありません。

| UTCの日付 | `mcp_request_timeout` の件数 | 内部待ち行列の期限切れ件数 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 2026-10-06 | 11 | 103 |
| 2026-10-07 | 48 | 200 |
| 2026-10-08 | 134 | 382 |

これらは内部RPCのログ件数であり、利用者の送信失敗件数や失われたメッセージ数ではありません。

14:42 JSTの確認時点では、128 GiBのRAMに対してスワップ使用量は0でした。アプリ関連プロセスのRSS単純合計は約18.9 GiBでした。共有ページを重複計上し得るため、この合計から実際の専有メモリ量やメモリリークの有無は判断できません。発生時のCPU負荷の実測値はありません。

関連する既存Issue：

- #52421、#52185：同じアプリバージョンで、非表示ウィンドウの同じ復帰イベントとACTIVE heartbeatとの関連が報告されています。
- #52093：Windowsの非表示Pagesウィンドウで同じイベントが大量発生する報告です。今回のmacOS環境でPagesのprewarmが原因だとは確認していません。
- #50812：Windowsで内部待ち行列のタイムアウト後に送信が失敗する報告です。今回も同じ内部機構が原因とは確定していません。

この報告の主題は、キューから送信されず、停止後の直接送信や分岐が必要になる操作上の問題です。既存Issueと同じ不具合であれば統合をお願いします。

認証情報、ローカルパス、チャットID、タスクID、業務の会話本文は省いています。スクリーンショットの背景に業務情報が含まれるため、画像や生ログは添付せず、必要なエラーと集計のみを記載しています。

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1002.52244 (build 13536); Codex Framework 155.0.8059.27

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro

### What platform is your computer?

Apple Silicon / arm64. uname -mprs: Darwin 25.6.0 arm64 arm. The sample report identifies macOS 26.7.1 (25G313); both diagnostics are included as reported.

### What issue are you seeing?

Codex (Renderer) continuously consumes over 100% CPU. I initially observed this with no tasks running. During subsequent diagnostic work, separate snapshots showed renderer CPU around 130–185%, and the ChatGPT main process around 40–87%; app-server CPU was substantially lower. These captures were taken while a troubleshooting conversation was active, not as an idle-only benchmark.

Fully quitting and relaunching the app does not resolve it. Force-quitting the affected renderer causes a replacement to appear and quickly return to over 100% CPU. The macOS Window menu lists only the current ChatGPT window.

Desktop logs flood with maybe_resume_skipped_inactive_hotkey_window: one captured interval contained 9,976 occurrences in approximately 1.378 seconds. The same conversation ID appears after restart. Window/renderer IDs change after recreation, but the event flood continues.

Example (conversation ID redacted):
```text
[electron-message-handler] maybe_resume_skipped_inactive_hotkey_window
conversationId=<redacted>
documentVisibilityState=visible
hostId=local
rendererWebContentsId=2
rendererWindowAppearance=primary
rendererWindowFocused=false
rendererWindowId=2
rendererWindowVisible=false
routePath=/index.html
```

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Reproduces on my existing installation:
1. Launch ChatGPT desktop with existing local state.
2. Leave it with no tasks running and observe sustained high CPU in Codex (Renderer).
3. Fully quit and relaunch: high CPU returns.
4. Force-quit the affected renderer: a replacement appears and high CPU returns.

I have not tested with a clean profile, so the original trigger is unknown.

### What is the expected behavior?

An idle desktop app should settle to low CPU usage. An inactive window should not repeatedly attempt to resume the same conversation thousands of times per second.

### Additional information

The repeated inactive-window resume events are a strong lead, but causality has not been proven. Hidden/prewarmed-window involvement is a hypothesis, not a confirmed root cause.

Related reports: #19916 and #20435. I have not tested whether disabling the popout shortcut affects this case. Also potentially related: #51401 (visible right-pane flickering and renderer respawn). This report adds a specific repeated inactive-window resume event; it is not yet established whether the root cause is the same.

labels.name: bug

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

App-reported version: 26.1002.52244, build 13536

### What subscription do you have?

using Premium seat for business under different email

### What platform is your computer?

- Windows 11 Home, version 10.0.26300, build 26300, x64

### What issue are you seeing?

On Windows 11, the bundled Node runtime and built-in browser tools fail during elevated sandbox setup, before the requested operation executes.

The sandbox log reports Windows error 32 while opening `node_repl.exe` for runtime read/execute validation at:

“open ACL target for root-only update”

The failure persisted after a Windows reboot. A harmless example.com test reproduced it before any Microsoft Planner access was attempted.

[OpenAI-Escalation-Evidence-09-10-2026.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33234930/OpenAI-Escalation-Evidence-09-10-2026.zip)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

unsure?

### What is the expected behavior?

to be able to have chatgpt open microsoft and other browsers in the app

### Additional information

## Summary

On Windows 11, the bundled Node runtime and built-in browser tools fail during elevated sandbox setup, before the requested operation executes.

The sandbox log reports Windows error 32 while opening `node_repl.exe` for runtime read/execute validation:

“open ACL target for root-only update”

The failure persisted after a Windows reboot. A harmless example.com test reproduced it before any Microsoft Planner access was attempted.

## Environment

Baseline collected before reboot:

- Windows 11 Home, version 10.0.26300, build 26300, x64
- Registered desktop package: OpenAI.Codex 26.1002.7124.0
- App-reported version: 26.1002.52244, build 13536, prod
- Bundled CLI: 0.162.0-alpha.2
- Runtime: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI\Codex\runtimes\cua_node\3dd31cfff853001c\bin\node_repl.exe`
- Effective task permissions: workspace-write, restricted networking
- Effective Windows sandbox backend: elevated

The saved `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"` was not the effective task permission profile. Different package/app version schemes are included for identification, not as evidence of a version mismatch.

## Reproduction

1. Open a local desktop task.
2. Invoke the connected `node_repl` tool with a harmless operation:

   nodeRepl.write('NODE_REPL_READ_ONLY_SMOKE_OK');
   nodeRepl.write(new Date().toISOString());

3. Alternatively, invoke the built-in browser:

   let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab(
     "iab",
     "https://example.com/",
     { visible: true }
   );

4. Sandbox setup fails before a success marker or browser state is returned.

## Post-reboot results

Observation date: 09/10/2026. Perth time is AWST, UTC+08.

Windows last boot:
- 11:57:28.500 AWST
- 03:57:28.500 UTC

Exactly one runtime test and one built-in browser test were performed after reboot.

Runtime test at 12:04:16–17 AWST / 04:04:16–17 UTC:

    node_repl kernel exited unexpectedly
    kernel_pid: 3392
    kernel_status: exited(code=1)
    kernel_stderr_tail:
    windows sandbox failed: helper_unknown_error: setup refresh had errors
    reason: stdout_eof
    stream_error: null

Built-in browser test, setup at 12:04:22.524 AWST / 04:04:22.524 UTC:

    trusted Node process exited unexpectedly; kernel reset, rerun your request

No manual reset or retry followed. No successful page read was demonstrated.

## Fresh log evidence

User-profile paths have been redacted:

    [2026-10-09T04:04:17.428694500+00:00]
    runtime read/execute validation failed:
    validate runtime read/execute access on
    <USERPROFILE>\AppData\Local\OpenAI\Codex\runtimes\cua_node\3dd31cfff853001c\bin\node_repl.exe:
    open ACL target for root-only update:
    The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process. (os error 32)

    [2026-10-09T04:04:17.442680+00:00]
    setup error: setup refresh had errors

The browser attempt recorded the same runtime validation error at
2026-10-09T04:04:22.589064600+00:00.

## File-use investigation

Read-only checks before reboot found:

- Windows Restart Manager identified six processes using the exact runtime executable. Their ancestry traced to the bundled Codex/ChatGPT app processes.
- This identifies file users, not a single exclusive lock holder.
- Read-data and attribute handle opens succeeded in the tested sharing combinations.
- WRITE_DAC-only and READ_CONTROL plus WRITE_DAC handle opens succeeded.
- FILE_WRITE_DATA-only open failed with error 32, even with full sharing.
- These were OPEN_EXISTING handle probes. No file data or ACLs were changed.
- Handle scans found no matching open file handles, but some processes were inaccessible.

These results are consistent with protection of a mapped executable, but do not establish the root cause or the sandbox helper’s actual requested access rights. The process information is pre-reboot evidence only.

## Impact

Local runtime and browser tools cannot initialise. Microsoft Planner cannot be read or updated through those tools.

The failure occurs before browser attachment or Microsoft authentication. It also reproduces against example.com, so it is not demonstrated to be Planner-specific.

## Expected result / request

Sandboxed runtime and browser tools should initialise successfully while the app’s own runtime processes are running.

Please investigate:

- The sandbox helper’s requested access mask and sharing flags when opening the runtime for ACL validation.
- Whether mapped executable protection explains the sharing violation.
- Why this failure recurs after reboot.
- A supported recovery procedure that preserves existing security settings, project files and chat history.

No configuration repairs, security changes, installations or Planner edits were performed during this investigation. The user performed the Windows reboot.

## Related report

https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/52404

That report describes the same runtime hash and error 32. It also includes a deny-read state parsing failure after app repair. That additional failure has not been observed in this investigation and is not claimed here.

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

Desktop app — Your dot / Dot conversation

### What feature would you like to see?

## Request

Please add a **Read aloud** action to completed messages from Dot in the desktop app. I want to choose an existing Dot message and listen to it without starting a live voice call or asking Dot to generate another response.

## Why this matters for Dot

Dot can send asynchronous updates, progress reports, questions, and longer answers while work continues. A message may already be waiting when I return. Listening to that exact message would make these updates easier to consume while multitasking or away from the keyboard.

A voice call serves a different interaction: it starts a live conversation. For this request, the text is already available; I only want audio playback of that selected message. Playback should not send a new prompt, regenerate the answer, or trigger more work.

## Proposed experience

- Add a speaker / Read aloud action in each completed Dot message’s action menu.
- Read the selected visible message, including earlier messages and asynchronous updates.
- Provide play, pause, resume, stop, and replay controls.
- Support playback speed controls and keyboard access.
- Keep playback explicitly user-initiated; incoming updates should not automatically speak.
- Handle code blocks and tool output sensibly, for example by allowing them to be skipped.

A simple per-message button would already meet the core need. This would improve accessibility and make Dot’s ongoing, asynchronous conversation easier to follow.

### Additional information

Related broader desktop requests: #20957 and #21645, plus Reader Mode discussion #38834.

This request makes the Dot conversation surface explicit, especially already-delivered asynchronous updates. Please ensure any shared desktop Read Aloud implementation also covers Dot messages. If this belongs under an existing tracker, please link or consolidate it while retaining the Dot-specific scope.

I could not find a Dot-specific issue in a search for is:issue label:dots "read" "aloud". This is a feature request, not a claim that Dot voice calls are broken.

### What issue are you seeing?

Codex Desktop suddenly stopped being able to access my project workspace, even though it had been working normally before.

Whenever I try to read project files or execute a command, the operation fails before the shell starts with this error:

```text
Failed to create unified exec process: helper_unknown_error: setup refresh had errors

The logs also contain the following error:

runtime read/execute validation failed: validate runtime read/execute access on C:\Users\Acer\AppData\Local\OpenAI\Codex\runtimes\cua_node\3dd31cfff853001c\bin\node_repl.exe: open ACL target for root-only update: The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process. (os error 32)
```

The setup refresh subsequently fails with:

```text
setup refresh completed with errors
setup error: setup refresh had errors
```

This prevents Codex from running basic commands such as `git status`, listing files, or reading source code. Retrying the commands does not resolve the problem.

The issue appears to occur during runtime or sandbox initialization, before the requested shell command can execute.


### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Feedback ID: 01a11f0a-efb5-7341-9137-753ad2c74653

### What is the expected behavior?

Codex should initialize its runtime and sandbox successfully, execute terminal commands, and read files from the selected project workspace.

A temporary runtime file lock should not leave the workspace permanently inaccessible. If initialization fails, Codex should provide actionable diagnostic information or recover automatically.


### Additional information

* Operating system: Windows (64-bit; exact Windows version to be provided).
* Codex version: 26.1002.52244.
* Runtime executable involved: `node_repl.exe`.
* Windows reports error 32, indicating that the file is being used by another process.

### Summary
A thread becomes permanently unopenable with `invalid paginated history lineage for <id>: cutoff byte offset is past the source rollout` when the base rollout shrank, even though `history_base.end_ordinal_exclusive` still identifies the correct cut point. Codex could recompute the byte offset from the ordinal (or offer a repair) instead of hard-failing.

### Environment
- Codex Desktop on Windows 11, local runtime 0.162.0-alpha.2; reproduced in a cloned CODEX_HOME with npm codex-cli 0.160.0 (`app-server` → `thread/resume`).

### What happened
- An external secret-redaction tool rewrote the base rollout in place (values replaced with shorter markers). Line count stayed the same (11,768 lines) but the file shrank by 3,429,307 bytes (54,218,237 → 50,717,700).
- The continuation segment's first line has `history_base = {end_ordinal_exclusive: 11761, end_byte_offset: 54147007}`. 54,147,007 > 50,717,700 → hard failure.
- The line at ordinal 11761 in the current base starts at byte 50,646,470. Replacing only `end_byte_offset` with that value (same byte length, rest of file unchanged) makes `thread/resume` succeed (`turns=20`). Verified first in a clone, then on the real file.

I understand the root trigger was an external edit; the request is for resilience/diagnostics.

### Expected
- On mismatch, recompute the offset from `end_ordinal_exclusive` when the line at that ordinal carries the matching `ordinal` field, or
- expose a supported repair/diagnostic (e.g. via `codex doctor`) instead of an unrecoverable error.

#41566, #47002, #41608

items.body:
### Summary
The `legacy_to_paginated_v1` rollout migration rewrote rollouts in place and, for rollouts whose `session_meta` has `thread_source: "subagent"` with `subagent_history_start_ordinal`, kept only the inherited prefix and dropped the thread's own history. Some of these were long-lived threads the user worked in directly. No backup was kept.

### Environment
- Codex Desktop on Windows 11; migration ran 2026-09-09 ~00:50–01:01 local time (`rollout-migrations/` dir created at 00:50, `rollout_migration_skipped_rollouts` row for `legacy_to_paginated_v1` stamped 01:01). Exact runtime version at that moment unknown (app logs before 09-24 were not retained).

### Evidence (counts only)
- 4,955 rollouts older than the migration have a CreationTime inside that window (rewritten in place).
- Of 1,511 pre-migration rollouts with `thread_source: "subagent"` + `subagent_history_start_ordinal`, only **2** keep any own lines dated before the migration. Lines before the start ordinal (inherited context) all carry the creation timestamp; lines after it start only after the migration date.
- **88** of them provably had activity before the migration (they spawned child threads then — `thread_spawn_edges`, children created in July/August), yet have zero own lines from that period. Examples: a thread that spawned 42 children from 2026-07-16 now contains its June prefix plus one turn from 10-08.
- Several affected threads have `source: "vscode"`, no parent edge, no `forked_from_id` — i.e. user-created threads labeled as subagents.
- `rollout-migrations/` is empty; no pre-migration copy exists. `thread_history_1.sqlite` kept serving the old items for a while; a later re-projection (first launch of a new build) removed them.
- Control: threads with `thread_source: "user"` (largest 240 MB) were migrated intact.

### Expected
- Never drop own history when migrating; verify the subagent classification before treating the prefix as the whole thread.
- Keep a backup (or reversible journal) of rewritten rollouts until the user confirms.

### Related
#35647 (forking writes full parent rollout into child JSONL), #44947

items.title: [Windows Desktop] Same thread id on local and SSH remote host: Desktop routes to the stale remote copy and never reconciles remote deletions

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: session
labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

items.body:
### Summary
When the same thread id exists on both the local host and an SSH remote host (`remote-ssh-discovered:*`), Codex Desktop routes the thread to the remote copy, and after the remote copy is deleted the desktop catalog never forgets it. Pinned threads became unopenable (`invalid paginated history lineage ...: missing source rollout`, `failed to resolve rollout path`, `no rollout found for thread id`) while their local rollouts were intact.

### Environment
- Codex Desktop on Windows 11 (26.1002.7124.0, then 26.1007.2314.0), local runtime 0.162.0-alpha.2
- SSH remote host (macOS) running codex-cli 0.160.0, connected via `remote-ssh-discovered`

### How the duplicate arose
A file-sync tool had copied the Windows host's `~/.codex/sessions` into the remote host's live `~/.codex/sessions` months earlier. The remote app-server registered those rollouts as its own threads (110 rows, `cwd` like `C:\...` or `/Users/<user>/C:\...`). So 92 thread ids existed on both hosts. (The sync was a user mistake; the issue is how Desktop resolves it.)

### Observed
1. `sqlite/codex-dev.db` → `local_thread_catalog` held two rows per id (`local` and the remote host). Opening a pinned thread routed to the remote host (log: `maybe_resume_started ... hostId=remote-ssh-discovered:...`), where the rollout no longer existed. The UI shows a globe icon but offers no way to choose the host.
2. Disconnecting the remote host made the same threads open locally — confirming routing, not data loss.
3. We removed the 92 rows on the remote with the official `thread/delete` (app-server JSON-RPC) while Desktop was closed. After reconnecting, Desktop still routed to the remote: the catalog is synced incrementally (`local_thread_catalog_sync_state.watermark_updated_at`) and deleted threads are never re-observed. `last_full_reconciled_at` for that host was 5 weeks old. Removing the stale catalog rows (app closed) fixed routing.
4. One local thread also had `thread-project-assignments` → remote project/host in `.codex-global-state.json`; it kept opening on the remote (`no rollout found for thread id`) until that assignment was removed.

### Expected
- For an id present on several hosts, prefer the host that actually has a readable rollout (or local), or let the user choose the host.
- Periodically reconcile the catalog against each host (drop rows the host no longer has), or react to `thread/deleted` on reconnect.
- A thread assigned to a remote project should not be routed to a host that does not have it.

### Related
#42628 (catalog retains deleted chats / missing rollouts), #44947, #34894

### What happens

Codex desktop repeatedly interrupts long-running local chats with HTTP 400 and only `{"detail":"Bad Request"}` in the response. This has affected more than one chat. Both ordinary model requests and remote compaction have failed, so compaction is not a reliable recovery path.

This is intermittent: an ordinary continuation later succeeded with the same active image history and without a new compaction. I do not have a deterministic minimal reproduction yet.

### Environment

- macOS, Codex desktop 26.1002.52244, build 13536, prod release channel.
- Bundled codex-cli: 0.162.0-alpha.2.
- Model: GPT-6.1 Sol; reasoning: high; service tier: priority.
- ChatGPT authentication; no custom model provider.
- The app updater reports `up_to_date` for the configured channel.
- Endpoint: `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses`.

### Failure and successful controls

All timestamps below are UTC on 2026-10-09. Sizes are reconstructed request-body sizes from the local diagnostic investigation, not server-side measurements.

| Result | Time | Request ID | Uncompressed bytes | Compressed bytes |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| HTTP 400 | 03:43:38 | d230fc23-9c96-4b94-81bf-4b97cad72522 | 16,200,440 | 8,778,325 |
| HTTP 200, immediately preceding request | 03:43:26 | 5f847219-4054-47b0-9c8b-e85e61226999 | 16,187,156 | 8,772,171 |
| HTTP 200, larger request | 03:38:02 | eb746e00-c745-4421-9944-4819b16979b1 | 25,071,411 | 18,597,014 |

At the latest failure, client logs reported:
- `auto_compact_scope_tokens=88921`.
- Auto-compaction threshold: 100000.
- `full_context_window_limit=258400`.
- Both token-limit-reached flags were false.

The larger successful request means a simple fixed 8 MiB request-size cutoff does not explain these observations.

Additional failures in the same chat occurred at 2026-10-08T21:03:20Z, 2026-10-09T02:09:24Z, and 02:09:58Z. At 02:25:37Z, the log specifically recorded `Error running remote compact task: {"detail":"Bad Request"}`. Successful compactions also occurred between these failures. Another local chat had HTTP 400 failures on October 7.

### Local checks and recovery observations

- The session JSONL parsed successfully.
- Checks of the five failure boundaries found correctly paired tool call/output IDs and no duplicate IDs.
- Relevant image encodings and image integrity checks passed.
- The latest failing active history contained 16 PNG images. The last addition before failure was approximately 8,145 characters of text, with no new image.
- An ordinary continuation between 04:02:30Z and 04:04:54Z succeeded without another compaction, while those 16 images remained in the active history.
- No environment HTTP/HTTPS/ALL proxy or enabled system HTTP proxy was found. A VPN extension is present; no VPN on/off comparison was performed.

### Separate explanation for apparently early compaction

A local troubleshooting workaround had explicitly set `model_auto_compact_token_limit=100000`. That explains compaction at approximately 39% of the 258400-token window. It did not prevent HTTP 400 and has been removed from the configuration. Existing running chats still showed the cached 100000 threshold; reload verification remains pending. I am not presenting that configured threshold as evidence of a default context-window defect.

### Expected behavior / requested investigation

Please correlate the failed and successful request IDs to identify the precise backend validation failure, including why a remote compaction can also receive the same generic 400. An actionable error and a supported recovery path would help avoid repeatedly interrupting long-running work.

The request-size and token observations above are evidence, not a confirmed root cause. No account credentials, raw request bodies, screenshots, project source, or complete session transcripts are included in this public report.

labels.name: bug

items.body:
## Summary

Local file-reading tools cannot initialize in Codex used through the ChatGPT desktop app on Windows. Two sandbox setup failures were observed during the same troubleshooting sequence:

1. A sharing violation (OS error 32) when validating read/execute access on `cua_node/3dd31cfff853001c/bin/node_repl.exe`.
2. After the user ran Windows app repair, `apply deny-read ACLs` failed with EOF while parsing `deny_read_acl_state.json`. Nearby subsequent refresh attempts still logged OS error 32.

The relationship between these failures is unknown. This report contains redacted diagnostic excerpts only.

## Environment

- Windows: Microsoft Windows 10 Home, version 10.0.19045, build 19045 (queried locally).
- Desktop surface: user reports using Codex inside the ChatGPT desktop app.
- Earlier app diagnostic reported version 26.1002.52244, build 13536. App version was not rechecked after repair.
- Bundled executable: `codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.2` (queried locally).
- Affected runtime: `%LOCALAPPDATA%/OpenAI/Codex/runtimes/cua_node/3dd31cfff853001c/bin/node_repl.exe`.
- Observation date: 2026-10-09.

## Observed reproduction

1. Open the desktop app and a local project.
2. Ask the agent to read a local instruction file through the connected `node_repl` tool.
3. The kernel exits before executing the requested read.
4. Resetting the tool, restarting the app, restarting Windows, and Windows app repair did not restore the tool.

The user explicitly verified that all four observed `node_repl.exe` processes disappear when the app exits. Thus leftover processes surviving app exit have not been established as the cause.

## Actual result

```text
node_repl kernel exited unexpectedly
kernel_status: exited(code=1)
kernel_stderr_tail:
windows sandbox failed: helper_unknown_error: setup refresh had errors
reason: stdout_eof
```

Redacted sandbox log excerpt, 2026-10-09:

```text
runtime read/execute validation failed:
validate runtime read/execute access on
%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI\Codex\runtimes\cua_node\3dd31cfff853001c\bin\node_repl.exe:
open ACL target for root-only update:
The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process. (os error 32)

setup error: setup refresh had errors
```

After app repair, another initialization attempt returned:

```text
windows sandbox failed: helper_unknown_error: apply deny-read ACLs

Caused by:
0: parse deny-read ACL state %USERPROFILE%\.codex\.sandbox\deny_read_acl_state.json
1: EOF while parsing a value at line 1 column 0
```

Nearby subsequent refreshes continued to report the executable sharing violation. The state file itself was not modified or inspected to establish its exact contents; the EOF evidence above comes from the setup log.

Ordinary sandboxed command startup also failed, while a separately approved command outside that sandbox successfully returned Node v24.18.0 and the bundled CLI version. An unrelated local Maker MCP connection continued to work. This suggests sandbox/tool initialization failure rather than failure to read one particular project file.

## Expected result / request

Sandboxed file-reading tools should initialize successfully, including while the app's own runtime processes are running. Please advise a supported repair procedure for both the executable ACL sharing violation and the deny-read state parsing failure, preserving existing permission boundaries, project files, and chat history.

No ACLs, deny-read state files, or sandbox policy were manually modified during these diagnostics. Full logs, private paths, project source, credentials, and sandbox secrets are intentionally omitted.

## Related reports

- #52172 and #52169: same runtime hash and OS error 32 after restart/reboot.
- #52389: executable-in-use ACL refresh failure.
- #34276 and #44034: deny-read state JSON parsing failures.

items.body:
## Environment

Browser-based ChatGPT Work at chatgpt.com, Chrome on Windows, managed Business/Team workspace as reported by the owner. Exact historical model, browser build and internal app/workspace binding have not been independently verified. This was not a local CLI action.

## Observed behavior

A GitHub create_blob tool request was rejected by automatic review. The submitted keys were repository_full_name, content and encoding. It was a UTF-8 blob-creation request, not a branch or commit update.

The retained request contains 17,218 bytes. The project's retained comparison and separate source decision identify those bytes as matching the approved artifact. The returned denial instead classified the payload as a different, previously rejected installer and insufficiently authorized.

That establishes an unresolved discrepancy in the retained evidence, not a confirmed reviewer defect: the internal comparison inputs are unknown. No request/correlation ID or created blob was returned.

The original browser conversation's inspected slash and More menus exposed no denied-action picker. Current documentation describes /approve in the open-source TUI, but does not establish a way to import or reconsider this browser event. A workspace confirmation preference was observed, but no historical-denial clearance was demonstrated.

The denied publications remain paused. No alternate execution route or repeat publication was attempted. Native and application acceptance are separately incomplete.

## Expected behavior / questions for maintainers

1. Identify the supported action-specific review/reconsideration route for an eligible browser Work denial.
2. If this denial is ineligible, explain the restriction and supported next step.
3. Correlate the original event privately and determine which submitted request and approved artifact identities were compared.
4. Clarify how to report a source-identity discrepancy when the returned denial contains no request ID.
5. Clarify the distinction between a read-only GitHub retrieval connection and the GitHub write-tool capability exposed in Work/Codex; do not infer the historical binding from either current capability metadata or generic retrieval documentation.

Private evidence is already available through an existing OpenAI Support case. It includes the conversation locator, reported timestamps, exact request identity, source decision and full denial. Repository names, source bytes, conversation URLs, account identifiers and hashes are intentionally omitted from this public report.

## Related reports, not established duplicates

- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/49239 — MCP write denied using disputed preflight interpretation; picker unavailable.
- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/50795 — desktop denial absent after CLI resume.
- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/50524 — policy rejection with no matching /approve entry.

## Official reference

https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/sandboxing/auto-review

No claim of a permanent account-wide ban, confirmed false positive, or guaranteed ability to override this denial is made.

items.title: Prevent sleep throughout an active goal, including between automatic turns

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: agent
labels.description: Issues related to the core agent loop

items.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

0.161.0

### What subscription do you have?

Business

### Which model were you using?

gpt-6.1-sol

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 27.0.1 (26A434)

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

IntelliJ IDEA 2026.2.3 integrated terminal

### Codex doctor report

Not collected for the recorded run. Only selected sanitized evidence is included below.

### What issue are you seeing?

Experimental prevent-sleep was enabled via `/experimental`. The Mac was connected to AC power, with its idle sleep timeout set to 10 minutes.

An unattended goal remained unfinished and eligible for automatic continuation, but macOS entered idle sleep after an intermediate turn released its sleep-prevention assertion. OpenVPN paused during sleep, and subsequent GitLab requests timed out. Codex eventually marked the goal blocked on connectivity.

Prevent-sleep should cover the lifetime of an actively pursued goal, including intervals between automatic turns and waits for background work.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Enable experimental sleep prevention.
2. Start a goal requiring multiple automatic turns, with background compilation or CI polling.
3. Leave the Mac unattended long enough to exceed its idle sleep timeout.
4. Observe sleep assertions and system sleep around intermediate turn completion:

   ```bash
   pmset -g assertions
   pmset -g log
   ```

This occurred in one recorded run; deterministic reproduction has not yet been established.

**Observed evidence**

Timeline from October 8, 2026, in UTC+02:00:

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 22:39:09 | Codex’s intermediate response reported that compilation was still running and the full goal remained active. |
| 22:39:09 | macOS logged Codex releasing `PreventUserIdleSystemSleep`, named `"Codex is running an active turn"`, with `[System: No Assertions]`. |
| 22:39:11 | OpenVPN logged `PAUSE sleep`. |
| 22:39:14 | The Codex transcript recorded the next automatic turn beginning. |
| 22:39:15 | macOS logged `Entering Sleep state due to 'Idle Sleep'`. |
| 23:47:42 | Codex reported the goal blocked after repeated private GitLab HTTPS and SSH timeouts. |

Live checks also confirmed that Codex processes launched from IntelliJ held system-wide sleep-prevention assertions during active turns.

The evidence suggests a protection gap or race around automatic continuation. It does not establish the exact implementation cause.

### What is the expected behavior?

With prevent-sleep enabled:

- Maintain sleep protection while a goal is active, including continuation transitions and background-work waits.
- Release goal-related protection when the goal completes, is paused, is cancelled, or becomes blocked and stops executing.
- Preserve protection while another goal or turn still needs it.
- Allow normal macOS idle sleep afterward; the display may turn off while work continues.

### Additional information

**Impact and workaround limitations**

Unattended goals can lose VPN connectivity and stop before completion.

Permanently disabling macOS sleep conflicts with the intended behavior: the Mac should sleep when Codex finishes working. Attaching `caffeinate` to the interactive Codex process has the same limitation because that process remains open after work ends.

**Validation requested**

Test continuation transitions after the system idle timeout has elapsed, including waits for background compilation or CI. Confirm that the Mac stays awake while the goal continues and can sleep after the last active goal or turn stops.

labels.name: bug

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Affected desktop session: **26.1002.6548.0**.
After the user-initiated update/restart: **26.1002.7124.0**.
Bundled/local app-server: **codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.2** before and after restart.

Versions were verified from the affected session's startup/update logs, the restarted session's logs, and the installed Windows package/runtime, rather than the About dialog.

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro ($200/month).

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 Pro, version 25H2, OS build **26200.9457**, x64.
Packaged application: `OpenAI.Codex`; desktop executable: `ChatGPT.exe`.

### What issue are you seeing?

On **October 8, 2026**, I watched a response being actively written in a desktop chat, then stepped away. When I returned after an unspecified interval, **the response was entirely missing from the chat**, not merely paused partway through writing.

I also noticed that Claude's attempt to run a delegated review had failed. I switched back to ChatGPT/Codex and clicked the app's **update button**. The application updated and restarted; logs place the new desktop process start at **20:33:56 MST (America/Phoenix)**.

**After restart, the full response was present. I did not send another message to the session to make it appear.**

The update button worked, so this report does not assert that the entire application UI was unresponsive. The exact time the response disappeared is unknown. Because the desktop build changed during this restart, the evidence cannot distinguish recovery due to the update from recovery due to restarting/reloading conversation state. It also does not establish when generation completed.

A read-only investigation found continued successful backend response routing before shutdown. This suggests a possible display or conversation-state synchronization problem, but the root cause is unconfirmed. A routed response does not prove renderer receipt or display, and the successful requests below are background/configuration requests, not proof that the affected response completed before restart.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

No deterministic reproducer is available. No reproduction was attempted during the investigation.

Observed sequence:

1. Use an existing desktop chat on build 26.1002.6548.0 and observe a response actively being written.
2. Step away for an unspecified interval.
3. Return and find that the previously visible response is entirely absent.
4. Click the app's update button; the app updates and restarts into build 26.1002.7124.0.
5. Observe the full response in the same chat without sending another message.

The exact disappearance time, affected-turn token/context utilization, and completion time were not established. Session identifiers and conversation content are omitted for privacy.

### What is the expected behavior?

A response that has already appeared should remain visible while generation continues and after generation completes. The desktop should reconcile the displayed conversation with stored/backend state without requiring an update or restart, and should show an actionable status if synchronization fails.

### Additional information

#### Timeline and diagnostic evidence

All times below are **October 8, 2026, MST (America/Phoenix)**. Log timestamps have been converted to local time; identifiers, private paths, and unrelated fields are omitted.

| Time (MST) | Observation |
| --- | --- |
| 08:16:09 | Affected desktop session started; its logs identify build 26.1002.6548.0 and local app-server 0.162.0-alpha.2. |
| 18:36:50 | First of five evening renderer ResizeObserver errors. |
| 18:42–19:25 | Four located Claude-delegated Codex CLI review sessions started, but execution tools failed during Windows sandbox setup. Details below. |
| 19:38:30–19:38:32 | The `durable` websocket disconnected with code 1006 and reconnected. This transient event does not establish a local app-server crash. |
| 20:14:14 | Last recorded evening ResizeObserver error. |
| 20:30:43 | Successful configuration responses still routed to desktop windows. |
| 20:33:38.997 | Desktop recorded `update_resume_state_saved`. |
| 20:33:50.131 | Last recorded pre-restart successful `skills/list` response; duration 1,127 ms, queue wait 0 ms. |
| 20:33:50 | Windows recorded the Codex sandbox service being asked to stop and stopping. |
| 20:33:56 | New desktop process started; sandbox service restarted. |
| 20:33:59–20:34:03 | New launch logged; successful backend requests followed. New desktop build was 26.1002.7124.0. |
| After restart; exact time unrecorded | User observed the full response without submitting another message. |

Selected sanitized excerpts:

```text
2026-10-08 18:36:50.168 MST
[desktop-notifications][global-error]
ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications.

2026-10-08 20:33:38.997 MST
update_resume_state_saved threadCount=0

2026-10-08 20:33:50.131 MST
[AppServerConnection] response_routed
method=skills/list durationMs=1127 queueWaitMs=0
errorCode=null targetDestroyed=false

2026-10-08 20:33:59.680 MST
Launching app ... packaged=true platform=win32

2026-10-08 20:34:00.075 MST
Current reported app-server version:
currentVersion=0.162.0-alpha.2 hostId=local
```

The inspected evening desktop main log, from approximately 17:00 through shutdown, contains **475 routed responses**, all with `errorCode=null`; recorded queue waits were **0–11 ms**. Five ResizeObserver errors were recorded, but their relationship to the missing response is unknown.

No `mcp_request_timeout`, `turn/start`, `spawn_agent`, six-slot queue-rejection/queue-expiration signature, or renderer-process termination was found in that evening main-log window. Absence from these logs does not rule out an unlogged failure.

No matching Application Hang, Application Error, or Windows Error Reporting record was found in the inspected evening window, and no relevant crash/hang dump was found. The sandbox-service events numbered 1000/1001/1002 were service lifecycle messages, not Windows application-crash events.

#### Separate, confirmed failure in delegated reviews

The delegated Codex CLI sessions **started**, but command creation failed during sandbox provisioning. This is not a recorded `spawn_agent` failure. The sandbox log contains **36 runtime-validation failures between 18:42:08 and 19:24:57 MST**, all targeting the same bundled `node_repl.exe`:

```text
2026-10-08 18:42:08.985 MST
runtime read/execute validation failed:
validate runtime read/execute access on
%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI\Codex\runtimes\cua_node\<runtime>\bin\node_repl.exe:
open ACL target for root-only update:
The process cannot access the file because it is being used
by another process. (os error 32)

2026-10-08 18:42:09.015 MST
exec_command failed: CreateProcess
Rejected("Failed to create unified exec process:
helper_unknown_error: setup refresh had errors")
```

This closely matches #51634, #52389, and #51590. It is included only because the user noticed both symptoms during the incident. **There is no established causal link between these sandbox failures and the response disappearing**, and their order relative to the disappearance is unknown. No historical blocking-handle trace identifies the particular holder.

#### Related issues and limitations

- #43460 is potentially related because backend replies can succeed while the desktop does not reflect them. This incident lacks that report's matched request/renderer-timeout pairs, so a duplicate is not established.
- #38385 describes six stuck requests and queue starvation; its defining signatures were not found here.
- #33524 shares ResizeObserver errors, but slow `thread/resume` evidence was not found here.
- #49611 describes runtime relocation failures; its `rename_staging`/`EPERM` signatures were not found here.

Accessible evidence included desktop logs, read-only app-server log-database queries, Codex session events, Claude delegation diagnostics, sandbox logs, Windows Application events, and WER/Crashpad/CrashDumps locations. Missing evidence includes a live hang capture, renderer-delivery trace, historical resource measurements, and the exact disappearance timestamp.

The investigation itself was read-only and did not change configurations, modify repositories, delete logs, restart processes, or attempt reproduction. The update/restart described above was performed by the user before the investigation. No raw logs, transcripts, source code, credentials, or identifying session data are attached.

### What issue are you seeing?

I frequently get the following error in Codex:

“Selected model is at capacity. Please try a different model.”

The issue happens very often when I run two Codex sessions concurrently. Once it starts, even a single Codex session can continue failing repeatedly with the same error for multiple requests in a row.

This is intermittent — sometimes Codex works normally for a while, but the problem keeps coming back.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Uploaded thread: 01a11eaf-c56f-7cc1-a6df-8a3aa60b2a65

### What is the expected behavior?

Codex should continue processing normal coding requests without repeatedly failing with a capacity error, especially when my usage quota is still available.

Running one or two normal Codex sessions should work reliably without triggering persistent “Selected model is at capacity” errors.

### Additional information

This issue has been happening for about 10 days.

I have contacted OpenAI Support multiple times, but the issue has not been resolved. I also logged out of all sessions and left the account unused for two full days before trying again, but the problem returned.

This Pro 20x account is used only by me and is not shared with anyone else. My usage is for normal, legitimate software development work.

Agent shell commands were rejected before the requested command could run. This affected even a simple read-only command:

/bin/bash -c pwd

The tool returned:

exec_command failed: CreateProcess { message: "Rejected(\"credential brokerage could not create a protected shell snapshot\")" }

I explicitly configured features.shell_snapshot = true, but the same error continued in my setup. Command execution recovered only after I disabled credential brokerage; the previously failing command then exited successfully.

The error provides no actionable explanation of whether snapshots are disabled in the effective session configuration, or whether capture, storage, or validation failed. 4. Disable credential brokerage and retry the same command. Execution subsequently succeeds.

### What is the expected behavior?

If refusing execution is intentional because a protected snapshot cannot be prepared, retain that safety check but provide actionable, credential-safe diagnostics to the user and agent. For example:

- State whether shell_snapshot is disabled in the effective runtime configuration.
- If it is enabled, distinguish capture, storage, timeout, or validation failure.
- Explain which setting or prerequisite should be checked and whether a new session is required.
- Suggest enabling shell_snapshot only when it is actually disabled.

The user or agent should receive useful guidance instead of only the generic rejection message. I am not requesting an unsafe fallback or automatic disabling of credential protection.

### Additional information

Related PR: openai/codex#43909 — “Protect shell snapshots when credential brokerage is enabled”.

I understand the security rationale for refusing execution when Codex cannot prepare a credential-safe snapshot. My concern is that the refusal also persisted after shell_snapshot=true was configured, and the error did not explain what remained wrong or how to investigate it.

A custom configuration-maintenance profile and a project-level .codex/config.toml symlink to its user-level source file were involved. I have not confirmed whether configuration layering, saved session settings, or app-server state contributed.

The CLI installation changed from 0.161.0 to 0.162.0 during troubleshooting. Disabling brokerage preceded recovery, but I have not performed a controlled comparison proving it was the sole cause.

I searched for the exact error before filing and did not find an existing matching user issue.

items.title: Add experimental app-server thread read-state updates
items.body:
Add experimental app-server thread read-state updates

## Why

Clients need to mark threads read or unread without overwriting unseen results or another window's explicit mark.

## What changed

Add `thread/readState/update` for eligible durable local threads, gated by `initialize.capabilities.experimentalApi`. Requests include `threadId`, `expectedRevision`, and an operation of `{type:"read"}` or `{type:"unread"}`.

Marking read clears `firstUnread`; marking unread sets it to `threadStart`. Successful updates return the read state and notify subscribers through `thread/readState/changed`. Both operations require an exact revision match. Stale requests return `-32600` with `readStateConflict` and the current read state, requiring a fresh user action rather than a blind retry. Updates do not change thread recency.

## Testing

Add app-server coverage for experimental capability gating, explicit unread marks and notifications, conflicts for both stale operations, and marking read with a fresh revision.
